record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: Characterize the two-dimensional achievement set E(p^n, q^n) for all parameters p, q in (0,1).

evidence.quote: Characterize E(p^n, q^n) for all p, q ∈ (0, 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a sequence $(v_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \|v_n\| < \infty$, define the (two-dimensional) achievement set
$$E(v_n) := \left\{\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n v_n : (\varepsilon_n) \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}\right\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2.$$
Fix $p, q \in (0,1)$ and let $v_n = (p^n, q^n)$. The set $E(p^n, q^n)$ is then a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

It is known that:
- if $\min(p,q) \le 1/2$, then $E(p^n,q^n)$ is homeomorphic to the Cantor set;
- if $p = q \ge 1/2$, then $E(p^n,q^n)$ is a line segment.

Problem: Give a complete topological/geometric characterization of $E(p^n, q^n)$ for every pair $(p,q) \in (0,1)\times(0,1)$. In particular, decide whether for every pair $p,q$ with $1/2 < q < p < 1$ the set $E(p^n,q^n)$ is homeomorphic to the Cantor set.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem. Partial results are known: $E(p^n,q^n)$ is a Cantor set when $\min(p,q)\le 1/2$, and is a line segment when $p=q\ge 1/2$. There is a conjecture that $E(p^n,q^n)$ is a Cantor set whenever $p>q>1/2$, but a full characterization for all $(p,q)\in(0,1)^2$ remains unresolved.
